To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
genetic polymorphsisms of N-acetyltransferase and glutathione-S-transferase have no independent effect, but modulate breast cancer susceptibility in the presence of other genotypes.
NAT1/NAT1 polymorphisms are not associated with breast cancer risk but that NAT2 polymorphisms may be associated with risk in postmenopusal women.

genetic polymorphims of N-acetyltransferase 1 and 2 have no independent effects on breast cancer, but they modulated breast cancer risk in combination of genetic polymorphisms with glutathione S transferase M1 and T1.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of NAT1/NAT 2 polymorphisms in the risk of breast cancer.
the genetic polymorphisms and their association with breast cancer in Korean women.
the role of NAT1, NAT2 and GSTM1, GSTT polymorphisms and their interaction with breast cancer in Korean women.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

NAT1, NAT2 and GSTM1, GSTT polymorphisms have no independent effect, but in the presence of both GSTM1, and GSTT1 gene deletion, NAT2 rapid acetylators are at an increased risk of developing breast cancer.
NAT1/NAT 2 polymorphisms do not have independent effects on breast cancer risk but they modulate the risk in the presence GSTM1 and/or GSTT1 null alleles.
the NAT1 and NAT1/NAT1, GSTM and GSTM/GSTT genotypes are not associated with breast cancer risk, and the NAT2 genotype may not be a risk factor for breast cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NAT1 and NAT1 and GSTM1 and NAT2 and GSTT1 polymorphisms have no independent effect but they modulate the breast cancer risk.
the GSTM1 and/or GSTT1 null genotype and the NAT2 rapid acetylating genotype are risk factors for breast cancer, while the NAT1 rapid genotype is not.
the combination of GSTM1, GSTT and NAT1 polymorphisms is associated with an increased risk of breast cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of NAT2 rapid and GSTM1 and/or GSTT1 null polymorphisms may be an important risk factor in breast cancer.
the combination of GST genotypes and NAT2 genotypes is associated with breast cancer risk.
genetic polymorphims of NAT1 and/or NAT2 may be important in the development of breast cancer in the presence of null GSTM1 and/or GSTT1.
